Series::StatAccessor::movmin¶

Back to Series::StatAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::StatAccessor::movmin() const
Series Series::StatAccessor::movmin(std::int64_t window) const
Series Series::StatAccessor::movmin(std::int64_t window, std::int64_t dim) const

Series SeriesStatProxy::movmin(std::int64_t window) const
Series SeriesStatProxy::movmin(std::int64_t window, std::int64_t dim) const

What It Does¶

movmin() emits the smallest value in each trailing window. It is the rolling low-water counterpart to movmax(): same shape, same partial-prefix startup, same default window three on the last axis.

Parameters And Return Shape¶

window is the maximum number of trailing positions and must be positive. dim selects the ordered axis, defaults to the last axis, and accepts negative indexing. Since each output selects an input value, shape and dtype are preserved.

Examples¶

Example 1. A low value remains active until it leaves the window.

auto rising = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0});
std::cout << rising.stat.movmin() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1, 1, 2]

Example 2. New lows replace the old low-water mark immediately.

auto mixed = pluss::make_series({3.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0, 0.0});
std::cout << mixed.stat().movmin(3) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[3, 1, 1, 1, 0]

In the rising series, value 1 remains in the first three windows. It leaves the window at the final position, so the minimum advances to 2.

Axis Example¶

auto x = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 2.0, 1.0}, {6.0, 5.0, 4.0}});
std::cout << x.stat.movmin(2, 1) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[3, 2, 1],
  [6, 5, 4]]

Each row is processed independently along dim=1.

Gradient And Ties¶

Each output sends sensitivity to its minimizing input. Equal minima divide that sensitivity evenly. Because windows overlap, one low value can collect gradient from several subsequent positions.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
x.stat.movmin(2).sum().reverse();
std::cout << x.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.5, 1.5, 0]

The first minimum contributes to the first 1; the tied second window divides its contribution; and the final window belongs to the second 1.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The operation returns values, not argmin positions.

  • Tied minima use an equal-share subgradient.

  • Omitted dim means the last axis; window must be positive.

See Also¶

  • movmax: trailing maximum.

  • movvar: trailing spread rather than an extreme.
